540945.l: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) (from cyto- 'cell' via Greek - 'container' + 'big, megalo-' + -virus via Latin 'poison') is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae. Humans and other primates serve as natural hosts. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans. Diseases associated with HHV-5 include mononucleosis and pneumonia, and congenital CMV in infants can lead to variety of birth defects, including those involving the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen.

540946.l: Aotine herpesvirus 1 (AoHV-1) is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540947.l: Cebine herpesvirus 1 (CbHV-1) is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540948.l: Cercopithecine herpesvirus 5 (CeHV-5) is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540949.l: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV), also called human herpesvirus 5 (HHV-5), is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, which in turn is a member of the viral family known as Herpesviridae or herpesviruses. It is also commonly called CMV. Within Herpesviridae, HCMV belongs to the Betaherpesvirinae subfamily, which also includes cytomegaloviruses from other mammals. CMV is a double-stranded DNA virus.

540950.l: Rhesus cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540951.l: Cynomolgus macaque cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540952.l: Drill monkey cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the family Orthoherpesviridae.

540953.l: Chimpanzee cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540954.l: Papiine herpesvirus 3 (PaHV-3) is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540955.l: Chacma baboon cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540956.l: Squirrel monkey cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Cytomegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540957.l: Roseolovirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae. There are six species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: HHV-6: sixth disease (roseola infantum, exanthema subitum); HHV-7: symptoms analog to the 'sixth disease'.

540958.l: Human herpesvirus 6A (HHV-6A) is a species of virus in the genus Roseolovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Herpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540959.l: Human herpesvirus 6B (HHV-6B) is a species of virus in the genus Roseolovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Herpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540960.l: Human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) is one of nine known members of the Herpesviridae family that infects humans. HHV-7 is a member of Betaherpesvirinae, a subfamily of the Herpesviridae that also includes HHV-6 and Cytomegalovirus (HHV-5 or HCMV). HHV-7 often acts together with HHV-6, and the viruses together are sometimes referred to by their genus, Roseolovirus. HHV-7 was first isolated in 1990 from CD4+ T cells taken from peripheral blood lymphocytes.

540961.l: Macaca nemestrina herpesvirus 7 is a species of virus in the family Orthoherpesviridae.

540962.l: Mouse thymic virus is a species of virus in the family Orthoherpesviridae.

540963.l: Porcine cytomegalovirus is a virus of the family Orthoherpesviridae. It causes a viral disease that is infectious to pigs.

540964.l: Muromegalovirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae. Rodents serve as natural hosts. There are three species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: infected peritoneal macrophages, dendritic cells (DC) and hepatocytes, inducing significant pathology in both the spleen and the liver. Murid viruses Murine cytomegalovirus and Murid herpesvirus 2 (MuHV-2) belong to this genus.

540965.l: Murine cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Muromegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540966.l: Murid herpesvirus 2 (MuHV-2) is a species of virus in the genus Muromegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540967.l: Murid herpesvirus 8 (MuHV-8) is a species of virus in the genus Muromegalovirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540968.l: Proboscivirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae. Elephants serve as natural hosts. EEHV1 causes asymptomatic infection in African elephants but causes fatal haemorrhagic disease in Asian elephants. The name "Proboscivirus" comes from the Greek word or "proboscis" meaning "the elephant trunk," for which the virus accordingly uses as a means of contraction and transmission (secretions or openings of the trunk) to enter the elephant's body.

540969.l: Elephant endotheliotropic herpesviruses (EEHV) are herpesviruses that infect elephants. They can cause a highly fatal hemorrhagic disease when transmitted to young Asian elephants. In African elephants, related forms of these viruses, which have been identified in wild populations, are generally benign, occasionally surfacing to cause small growths or lesions. However, some types of EEHV can cause a highly fatal disease in Asian elephants, which kills up to 80% of severely affected individuals. The disease can be treated with the rapid application of antiviral drugs, but this has only been effective in around a third of cases.

540970.l: Elephant endotheliotropic herpesvirus 4 is a species of virus in the genus Proboscivirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540971.l: Elephant endotheliotropic herpesvirus 5 is a species of virus in the genus Proboscivirus, subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540972.l: Quwivirus is a genus of viruses in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, in the family Orthoherpesviridae, in the order Herpesvirales.

540973.l: Guinea pig cytomegalovirus is a species of virus in the genus Quwivirus, in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540974.l: Miniopterus schreibersii herpesvirus is a species of virus in the genus Quwivirus in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540975.l: Tupaia herpesvirus is a species of virus in the genus Quwivirus in the subfamily Betaherpesvirinae, family Orthoherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540977.l: Acciptrid herpesvirus 1 (AcHV-1) is an unaccepted species of virus suggested to belong to the order Herpesvirales and family Herpesviridae. It was isolated from a bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus).

540978.l: Agua Preta virus is an unaccepted species of virus, suggested to belong to the order Herpesvirales and family Orthoherpesviridae, as determined by thin-section electron microscopy. It was isolated from the gray short-tailed bat, Carollia subrufa, in the Utinga Forest near Belém, Brazil.

540979.l: Iguanid herpesvirus 2 (IgHV-2) is a species of virus of uncertain generic and subfamilial placement in the family Herpesviridae and order Herpesvirales.

540980.l: Alloherpesviridae is a family of viruses in the order Herpesvirales. This family includes the species that infect fish and amphibians. Phylogenetic studies have confirmed the validity of this family and suggest that it may be divided into two clades: one consisting of viruses from cyprinid and anguillid hosts and the other of viruses from ictalurid, salmonid, acipenserid, and ranid hosts. The family has four genera. A disease associated with this family is channel catfish disease.

540981.l: Cyvirus, previously named Cyprinivirus, is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Alloherpesviridae. Freshwater eels serve as natural hosts. There are four species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: hemorrhagic disease.

540982.l: Anguillid herpesvirus 1 (AngHV1) is a species of virus in the genus Cyvirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540983.l: Cyprinid herpesvirus 1 (CyHV1) is a species of virus in the genus Cyvirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540984.l: Cyprinid herpesvirus 2 (CyHV2) is a species of virus in the genus Cyvirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540985.l: Koi herpesvirus (KHV) is a species in the genus Cyvirus, the family Alloherpesviridae, and the order Herpesvirales. It causes a viral disease that is very contagious to the common carp Cyprinus carpio.

540986.l: Batravirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Alloherpesviridae. Frogs serve as natural hosts. There are three species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: raHV-1: Lucké tumor (renal adenocarcinoma).

540987.l: Ranid herpesvirus 1 (RaHV-1), is a double-stranded DNA virus within the order Herpesvirales. The virus was initially observed within renal tumors in 1934 by Baldwin Lucké, and more recently has become identifiable through the use of PCR in samples isolated from frog tumors. RaHV-1 causes renal tumors within the northern leopard frog, Rana pipiens. The virus has not yet been isolated in vitro within cell lines, meaning that while its existence and symptoms are fairly evident, its methods of transmission, cell infection, and reproduction are largely unknown.

540988.l: Ranid herpesvirus 2 (RaHV-2) is a species of virus in the genus Batrachovirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540989.l: Ranid herpesvirus 3 (RaHV3) is a species of virus in the genus Batravirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540990.l: Ictavirus, formerly called Ictalurivirus, is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Alloherpesviridae. Fish serve as natural hosts. There are three species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: channel catfish disease.

540991.l: Acipenserid herpesvirus 2 (AciHV2) is a species of virus in the genus Ictavirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales. It infects sturgeon of the family Acipenseridae.

540992.l: Channel catfish virus (CCV) is a species of virus in the genus Ictavirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales. It causes disease in channel catfish and blue catfish, and can cause significant economic loss in catfish farms. The disease is endemic in the USA and there are reports of the virus in Honduras and Russia.

540993.l: Ictalurid herpesvirus 2 (IcHV2) is a species of virus in the genus Ictavirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales.

540994.l: Salmovirus, previously called Salmonivirus, is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, in the family Alloherpesviridae. Salmonidae serve as natural hosts. There are three species in this genus. Diseases associated with this genus include: SalHV-3: epizootic epitheliotropic disease.

540995.l: Salmonid herpesvirus 1 (SalHV1), also called Herpesvirus salmonis, is a species of virus in the genus Salmovirus, and family Alloherpesviridae.

540996.l: Oncorhynchus masou virus (OMV), also called Salmonid herpesvirus 2 (SalHV2), is a species of virus in the genus Salmovirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales. The virus causes Oncorhynchus masou virus disease (OMVD), first described in 1981.

540997.l: Epizootic epitheliotrophic disease virus (EEDV), also called Salmonid herpesvirus 3 (SalHV3), is a species of virus in the genus Salmovirus, family Alloherpesviridae, and order Herpesvirales. The virus causes epizootic epitheliotrophic disease (EED), first described in 1989.

540998.l: Malacoherpesviridae is a family of DNA viruses in the order Herpesvirales. Molluscs serve as natural hosts, making members of this family the only known herpesviruses to infect invertebrates. There are currently only two species recognised in this family, both classified into separate genera. Disease associated with this family includes sporadic episodes of high mortality among larvae and juveniles. The family name Malacoherpesviridae is derived from Greek word 'μαλακός (malacos) meaning 'soft' and from Greek word 'μαλάκιον (malakion) meaning 'mollusc'.

540999.l: Aurivirus is a genus of viruses in the order Herpesvirales, and one of only two genera the family Malacoherpesviridae. Haliotid molluscs serve as natural hosts. There is only one species described in this genus, Aurivirus haliotidmalaco1, also called Haliotid herpesvirus 1 (AbHV-1) and commonly known as abalone herpesvirus. A disease associated with this virus is acute ganglioneuritis.
